prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1002; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling through the intersection in Sugar Land, Texas, and was turning left when the vehicle was struck by Driver 2, who was proceeding straight through on the same roadway. Driver 1 stated that the impact was forceful and that they felt an immediate jolt to the neck and upper back, later reporting whiplash symptoms. The nature of the collision and the force involved appear consistent with the reported injury. Damage to the front driver side of Driver 1's vehicle and the rear of Driver 2's vehicle matches the impact described by both parties. Photographs taken at the scene confirm the general position of both vehicles and the damage observed. No independent witnesses were located, so the account rests on the statements of the drivers and the photographs. A Passenger was also present in Driver 1's vehicle; responding officers and the witnesses who were interviewed confirmed that Passenger was seated inside at the time of the collision. Some minor scratches on the lower bumper area appear to be older than this incident and were noted separately. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the insurance policy covering the vehicle.
